subject: Columbus School Renaming Evaluation Rubric
overview: The committee introduced its members and established the formal process for vetting name submissions for the former Columbus Elementary School. They adopted a scoring rubric and a protocol for narrowing the current list of 84 names down to three finalists.

items.title: Introductions and Committee Charge
items.summary: Committee members introduced themselves and reviewed the School Committee's guidelines for recommending three new names for the school by late May.

items.title: Resolution to Adopt Evaluation Rubric
items.summary: The committee debated and adopted a formal resolution outlining a scoring rubric and a multi-step process for evaluating and narrowing name submissions. The resolution requires that 15 semi-finalists receive the highest average scores from five randomly assigned committee members before consideration by the full body.

items.title: Amendment on Nominating Living Persons
items.summary: The committee rejected an amendment to allow the naming of the school after a living person, upholding the original restriction that nominees must be deceased.

items.title: Rubric Clarification for Non-Person Names
items.summary: The committee accepted friendly amendments to the rubric to provide specific scoring criteria for submissions that are concepts or locations rather than individuals.

items.title: Timeline Extension Discussion
items.summary: A motion to request a one-week timeline extension from the School Committee was withdrawn after members discussed the necessity of aligning the renaming with end-of-year school ceremonies.

items.title: Protocol for Cleaning and Assigning Names
items.summary: The committee approved an administrative task for a subgroup to remove obvious exclusions—including variations of Christopher Columbus and bad-faith entries—and randomly assign the remaining valid names to members for scoring before the next meeting.
